To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the transcriptome of bull spermatozoon was analysed for the first time; 2) 415 transcripts were differentially detected between high- and low-fertility bulls; 3) the spermatozoa of high-fertility bulls contain higher concentration of transcripts related to the membrane and extracellular spaces, while spermatozoon from low-fertility bulls are deficient of transcripts related to transcription and translation; 4) quantitative PCR was used to validate the microarrays data and

(i) spermatozoa contain remnant messenger RNA; (ii) the RNA profiles of sperm cells from high-fertility (HF) bulls were different from those from low-fertility (LF) bulls; (iii) HF bulls had a greater number of transcripts associated with membrane and extracellular locations; and (iv) LF bulls had lower levels of transcripts associated with transcription and translational factors.
